procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Postpartum check-in, 12 weeks after 2nd delivery (NSVD 10/17/25).

Doing well. Baby exclusively breastfed, gaining well per pediatrics. No breast redness, lumps or fevers this time. Sleeping in chunks. Back to school after February break.
Addison's: on HC 20/10, fludro 0.1. Stress dosing in labor went per plan; back to usual doses since 10/19. No lightheadedness.
OB postpartum visit 12/3: diastasis recti, no hernia, PT referral - first PT appointment next week.
Meds also folic acid. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight still above pre-pregnancy. Comfortable. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen: midline separation above umbilicus with head lift, nontender, no hernia. Breasts not examined.
PHQ-9 2.

A/P
1. Postpartum, doing well; mood screen negative.
2. Primary adrenal insufficiency - stable. BMP today. Endo f/u 2/9.
3. Diastasis recti - PT as planned.
4. CBC today (postpartum).

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient Physical Therapy - Pelvic Health / Initial Evaluation, 01/20/2026
Referral: OB/GYN, dx diastasis recti abdominis

Subjective: 34 y.o., 3 months postpartum (2nd vaginal delivery), breastfeeding. Notices a midline bulge with sitting up and lifting her baby and car seat. No pain. No urinary leakage or pelvic heaviness. PMH: primary adrenal insufficiency on hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone. NKDA. Goals: lift kids and return to yoga without doming.

Objective: supine curl-up produces midline doming above the umbilicus; separation palpable along the linea alba above the umbilicus, softer tension at the umbilicus, no hernia. Pelvic floor screen normal. Lumbar ROM full.

Assessment: diastasis recti abdominis with impaired deep core recruitment and load transfer. Good rehab potential.

Plan: 1x/week for 8 weeks - breath and transversus abdominis activation, graded loading, lifting mechanics, home program. Avoid full sit-ups/crunches for now.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up - 2/9/2026

Dear Colleague,

Kayla is almost four months postpartum after her second delivery, which went smoothly with the intrapartum stress-dose plan. She is exclusively breastfeeding and feels well. No crises, no injections used. Electrolytes and renin from 2/2 are in range, and BP is normal without orthostasis.

Medications: hydrocortisone 20 mg on waking, 10 mg early afternoon; fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily; folic acid. NKDA.

Plan: no change to her doses. Both medications remain fine with breastfeeding. Annual TSH via your office. New emergency vial sent; her current one expires in May. I'll see her in 5-6 months.

With thanks

documents.title: Prior Authorization - Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy says new emergency vial from endo (sent 2/9) needs PA again for 2026. Submitted with endo letter 2/9/26 and dx code. Approved 2/16/2026, 12 months. Pt notified via portal she can pick it up.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient Physical Therapy - Discharge Summary
Dates of care: 01/20/2026 - 03/23/2026, 8 visits
Diagnosis: diastasis recti abdominis

Progress: independent with home program. Improved deep core activation and breath control with lifting; doming with curl-up reduced. The midline bulge is still present with exertion but smaller and better controlled. No pain. No hernia noted at any visit. Has resumed gentle yoga with modifications.

Plan: discharge to home exercise program. May return with new referral if symptoms worsen.

documents.title: Pumping at school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Baby turned 6 months and we started solids this week. I'm back at school and pumping twice a day. The nurse's office asked whether pumping in the afternoon is okay with my afternoon hydrocortisone dose. I assume yes?

documents.title: RE: Pumping at school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, totally fine - very little hydrocortisone gets into milk at your dose and no timing changes are needed. Keep taking it around 2 PM as usual. Happy 6 months to the baby!

documents.title: Medication Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refills due: hydrocortisone 20 mg, hydrocortisone 10 mg, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg, 90-day. Pharmacy confirmed she picked up the new emergency vial from endo in February.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology - 07/13/2026

Autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency, diagnosed 12/2022. Feels well this summer. Still nursing her 9-month-old alongside solids. No stress-dosing episodes since delivery. Emergency kit current.

Meds: hydrocortisone 20 mg / 10 mg, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg. NKDA.
Exam: BP normal, no postural drop. No hyperpigmentation.
Labs today: sodium and potassium normal; renin in range.

Plan: continue present doses. Follow up in 6-9 months.

conditions.label: Exclusive breastfeeding
conditions.note: Solids since about 6 months (April 2026); still nursing

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 34F.

Interval since last physical (8/2024): second pregnancy and uncomplicated vaginal delivery 10/17/2025 with intrapartum stress dosing; postpartum diastasis recti, finished PT in March and doing her home program - bulge smaller, no pain. Baby is 10 months, on solids since April, still nursing morning and night and pumping once at school.
Addison disease: endo 7/13, unchanged. No sick-day episodes this year.
Meds: hydrocortisone 20 mg on waking, 10 mg ~2 PM; fludrocortisone 0.1 mg; folic acid 0.4 mg; HC sodium succinate 100 mg IM kit (in date). NKDA.
Never smoker. No alcohol.

ROS: negative. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted; weight down since January, close to pre-pregnancy. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Breasts: healed R UOQ scar, no masses. Abdomen: small midline separation above umbilicus with head lift, nontender, no hernia. Skin: no abnormal pigmentation. Ext no edema.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune - stable. TSH, CMP today.
2. Exclusive breastfeeding ended with solids; continues nursing. Folic acid while nursing is fine.
3. Diastasis recti - home program.
4. HM: Pap/HPV due 2027. Lipids today. Flu shot booked for October; COVID when the new vaccine is out.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kayla, labs from Monday are all normal - thyroid, blood count, electrolytes, kidney and liver function, and cholesterol. Nothing to change. Good luck with the start of school!

documents.title: School Emergency Letter
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called: school nurse needs an updated adrenal insufficiency emergency action letter for the new school year. Last year's template updated by PCP with current doses and emergency injection instructions, signed, and emailed to pt via portal; copy scanned.
